history.name: The authoring rules
history.description: The command ledger rules prints the full rules for writing the ledger: what each field means, where the bar for an entry sits, how to record a change or a removal, and which parts of the corpus you edit by hand instead. The project's tone is printed inside it, and a RULES.md in the ledger directory replaces the packaged text with your own house conventions.

The command ledger rules prints the rules for recording what the product does: the bar for an entry, how to name one, how to record a capability, a change or a removal, and what you edit by hand instead. The project's tone is printed inside it, and a RULES.md in the ledger directory replaces it.

events.what: The rules describe a change as what moved and why, the code each entry lives in, and editing the composed notes, and no longer teach how to write a client-facing note mid-release.
events.why: Those rules existed to keep mid-release notes honest, and the notes are composed now. An agent reads the rules before its first edit, so every line it doesn't need is paid for on every edit.

events.what: The rules cover only what an agent recording a change needs.
events.why: Every task asked the agent to read the full rules first, and at 30 KB most of it was irrelevant to the task.
